answers: Noticed Pete Davidson's absence from SNL as of late? Well, there's a good reason behind it: The 23-year-old has been focusing on his sobriety. After telling High Times last fall that he couldn't function without the medical marijuana he's prescribed for Crohn's disease, Davidson now says, "I quit drugs and am happy and sober for the first time in eight years" in an Instagram post. Rapper Kid Cudi might have inspired that sobriety, per the New York Daily News. Last fall, Davidson told a radio station, "I would have killed myself if I didn't have Kid Cudi," who'd checked himself into rehab a few weeks earlier.

full.prediction:
**Summary of News on Pete Davidson**

Pete Davidson, a cast member of *Saturday Night Live* (SNL), has been in the spotlight for his candid discussions about his use of medical marijuana and his journey toward sobriety. In a recent interview with *High Times*, Davidson spoke openly about how he uses cannabis to manage his Crohn’s disease, a chronic condition he was diagnosed with at a young age. He criticized the New York State medical marijuana program for being difficult to access and expressed frustration with those who oppose the legalization of cannabis, stating, “I wouldn’t be able to perform on SNL if I couldn’t smoke weed!”

Davidson has also been vocal about his belief in the broader legalization of cannabis, not just for medical purposes. Despite his public advocacy, he has faced challenges in maintaining a consistent performance due to the effects of cannabis on his health. He has shared that without it, he struggles to function, both physically and creatively. “Me performing not high has gone awful,” he said, emphasizing the importance of cannabis in his ability to work.

In a recent social media post, Davidson announced that he has been sober for the first time in eight years. He shared that he quit drugs and is now in a healthier, more stable place in life, thanks to the support of his girlfriend, friends, and fans. He expressed gratitude for the love and encouragement he has received and encouraged others not to give up hope, stating, “We are a family and I appreciate all your love and support.”

Davidson has also credited Kid Cudi’s music for playing a significant role in his recovery. He shared that the rapper’s music helped him through a difficult time and that Cudi’s own struggles with mental health made him a relatable figure. “He saved my life. I would have killed myself if I didn’t have Kid Cudi,” Davidson said, highlighting the impact of music and personal connection in his journey.

Despite his public struggles, Davidson remains a prominent figure in the entertainment industry. He is set to debut his first hour-long stand-up special, “SMD,” on Comedy Central, and Season 42 of *Saturday Night Live* is set to premiere on NBC. His openness about his health, sobriety, and advocacy for cannabis has made him a unique and influential voice in both comedy and the ongoing conversation around medical marijuana and drug policy.
